author: WP08
summary: Defines the internal renderer contract: default-body kinds, resource ownership, null factories, borrowed handles, the presentation, swap-interval, format and readback matrices, resource and draw defaults, targets, clears, viewport and scissor, capability polarity and recovery hooks. About half of its family rows were stale at 009d40f5 (moves now transfer registration, rebinding is a no-op, clears throw on missing aspects, readback is HiDef-only and refused while a target is bound, many listed defects fixed). The site had strong device and resource internals but no consolidated contract, presentation or clear/viewport matrix; three deep dives now carry it.

concepts.text: Every renderer family implements one internal C++ contract, and the contract is deliberately permissive: methods may be pure virtual, return null, throw, forward to a reduced operation or do nothing, so reaching an interface method is no evidence that the selected family performed the work.
tokens: Reaching an interface method therefore says nothing

target.evidence: modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp (default bodies of IGraphicsRenderer and the resource interfaces)

concepts.text: Cross-family observations from a retained multi-product audit are historical where they were not rerun; a family absent from such a cohort means not measured, not unsupported, and a former text-mode renderer survives only as the CNAEXT AsciiPostProcessEffect.
concepts.note: Framing of an older audit campaign; its per-family rows were re-verified family by family at 009d40f5 in the concepts below rather than carried over.

concepts.text: The whole contract is one header, IGraphicsRenderer.hpp; at 009d40f5 it declares seventeen interface classes (buffers, textures, volume and cube textures, render targets, effects, occlusion queries, SpriteBatch, the CNAEXT modern surface of GPU timers, storage buffers, compute, texture arrays and storage textures, the thread-context lease and IGraphicsRenderer itself), not eleven.
concepts.note: Older text listed eleven interfaces; the modern-surface and lease interfaces were added through the same header.

concepts.text: Pure-virtual members force a decision: CreateTexture, CreateSpriteBatch, CreateVertexBuffer, CreateIndexBuffer16, SetRenderTargets, the seven clear entry points, DrawColoredPrimitives, SetVirtualResolution, SetPresentationMode, SetVertexDeclaration and the core effect and sprite methods; SetVertexDeclaration and SetRenderTargets were made pure so a new family cannot silently discard a declaration or flatten a cube face.
Null-factory defaults cover volume and cube textures, render targets, effect renderers, occlusion queries, compiled effects and every modern-surface factory; the public result depends on the wrapper.

Silent no-op defaults cover the state setters, blend factor, reference stencil, scissor, viewport, swap interval, recovery policy, string markers, the debug loss hooks, DispatchCompute, effect uniform and texture setters and SpriteBatch sampler options, so a successful call and a stored public value may have no native effect.

Reduced-fallback defaults complete work while discarding part of the request: effect-aware draws call the coloured draw, SetDataWithOptions drops the option, the render-target EXT factories drop the SurfaceFormat and the sub-pixel sprite Draw truncates to whole pixels.
tokens: truncates the destination to whole pixels
concepts.note: Added the sub-pixel sprite and render-target format fallbacks that exist at 009d40f5.

concepts.text: Throwing defaults: ReadBackbuffer, DrawInstancedPrimitivesEx, both indirect draws, CreateIndexBuffer32 and SetData32 throw std::runtime_error, while texture GetData and cube/volume transfers return false and the public wrappers turn that into NotSupportedException, so exception type and timing vary.
Treat every optional method as an independent capability: a non-null renderer object, a true capability answer and one successful draw are different facts.
tokens: Treat every optional method as its own capability

concepts.text: Which reduced fallbacks are reachable: every 3D-capable family overrides both effect-aware draws, so only STUB reaches the coloured fallback; only EasyGL, OpenGL4 and Software override the sub-pixel sprite draw; Vulkan inherits the option-dropping SetDataWithOptions and WebGPU's override ignores the option.
concepts.note: Post-Phase-3 adversarial audit correction: an override is not honouring: only DirectX 9, DirectX 11, EasyGL, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU and FNA3D turn Discard and NoOverwrite into different native operations; the destination now says which (C05 ch19-F1).

concepts.text: A public GraphicsResource owns its renderer handle (unique_ptr for most resources, shared_ptr for Texture2D so value copies share one renderer object); the device owns neither and keeps raw GraphicsResource addresses only for disposal order, with a weak lifetime token in each resource.

GraphicsDevice::Dispose marks the device disposed, raises Disposing (explicit disposal only), then moves and clears the registry and disposes each resource, and only then destroys the renderer, presenter and window, so re-entrant deregistration is harmless.
tokens: Raise Disposing, only for an explicit disposal
concepts.note: The source raises Disposing before disposing resources, not after.

concepts.text: Moving a buffer, texture or render target transfers the device registry entry (TransferResourceReference, TransferMovedTexture) and marks the moved-from object disposed; the claim that moves leave the device tracking the moved-from value is false at 009d40f5.
concepts.note: Moves transfer the registry entry at 009d40f5; the page states the current rule instead.

concepts.text: A Texture2D copy is not registered with the device, has its own disposed flag and shares the renderer object, so a copy that outlives the device can release the renderer object after the family is gone; dispose every alias before the device (Vulkan disconnects survivors in its destructor).
tokens: dispose every alias before the device

concepts.text: Keep live graphics resources device-scoped and do not keep objects alive across an explicit device disposal.

CNA's docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md says destructor cleanup suppresses ResourceDestroyed, but GraphicsResource::Dispose(false) still raises the device's ResourceDestroyed when the device is alive.
concepts.note: A documentation-staleness note about a CNA Markdown file, not a runtime fact; GraphicsResource::Dispose(bool) at 009d40f5 calls OnResourceDestroyed whenever the lifetime token is alive. Recorded as a not-an-issue candidate.

concepts.text: OcclusionQuery no longer constructs an inert object: construction throws NotSupportedException under Reach, when the OcclusionQuery capability is false, or when the capability is true but the factory returned null.
tokens: there is no inert query object any more
concepts.note: Older text: a null query constructed and answered incomplete/zero.

concepts.text: Texture3D refuses construction when the Texture3D capability is false; with a true capability and a null factory it constructs, and SetData/GetData then throw NotSupportedException instead of silently doing nothing.

TextureCube constructs with a null renderer (no cube capability exists) and its transfers throw NotSupportedException naming the missing cube-map resource; cube and volume transfers never fabricate or discard content.
tokens: this renderer creates no cube-map resource

concepts.text: RenderTarget2D and RenderTargetCube construct with a null renderer by design; binding throws NotSupportedException inside SetRenderTargets before any public binding state changes, and data transfers refuse likewise.

The singular SetRenderTarget(rt) path formerly passed a null target renderer through as a restore-back-buffer request while recording the target as bound; it now routes through SetRenderTargets and refuses.

Which families keep the null defaults has changed: at 009d40f5 Software has real occlusion queries, volume storage and cube targets; PORTABLEGL and STUB keep the null render-target and occlusion-query defaults, and some 2D families override a factory only to refuse.
tokens: keep the null render-target and occlusion-query defaults
concepts.note: Older text said Software inherited null volume, cube-target and query factories.

concepts.text: DirectX 9 can return null factory results according to device capabilities.
tokens: a family may also override a factory only to refuse
concepts.note: Stated generically on the page (families may override only to refuse); the DirectX 9 device-capability branches were not traced.

concepts.text: ShaderEffect::SetTexture for TextureCube and Texture3D passes texture.GetRenderer(), which dereferences the renderer handle unconditionally, so a cube or volume texture whose factory returned null cannot safely be handed to a ShaderEffect.
No individual capability value covers every texture and target factory; construction alone does not establish usable storage.
tokens: No capability value covers every texture and target factory

concepts.text: The framework needs one consistent null-factory policy; at 009d40f5 it is largely unified around refusal at the first operation that needs storage (early refusal for OcclusionQuery and capability-gated Texture3D).
tokens: The null default is not one failure policy

concepts.text: The renderer interface no longer has pure-virtual accessors that hand out toolkit window or renderer pointers; a family receives an immutable RendererSurfaceInfo snapshot (WindowId, typed NativeWindowHandle, drawable size, display scale) that owns nothing.
tokens: describe an API that no longer exists
concepts.note: The older accessor pair does not exist at 009d40f5.

concepts.text: Do not destroy or cache a borrowed window across device disposal; GameWindow receives a borrowed IPlatformWindow* once in the Game constructor and nothing clears it when the game explicitly disposes the device.
concepts.note: The facade now holds a platform window pointer, not a toolkit window.

concepts.text: The typed GameWindow::GetNativeWindowHandleEXT() and the integer XNA Handle property expose the platform window without transferring ownership.
concepts.note: The SDL-typed accessor was replaced by a platform-neutral one.

concepts.text: PresentationParameters::DeviceWindowHandle is an integer token interpreted only by the active platform (AdoptWindowHandle); CNA never destroys or recreates such a window and skips an incompatible fallback candidate with WindowKindConflict.
concepts.note: The value is no longer reinterpreted as a toolkit window pointer by GraphicsDevice.

concepts.text: An adopted window is published to the global TextInputEXT and Mouse window slots, and teardown clears each slot only if it still names this device's window; the slots have last-writer semantics so two live devices replace each other's input target, and no test covers that.

concepts.section: Presentation and input are family contracts
concepts.text: The public device stores one presentation request and the selected family decides whether it changes a compositor, a swapchain, a CPU buffer, only reported state or nothing; Game builds its device with defaults and the manager applies preferences later through Reset.

Window-to-logical input goes through a WindowId-keyed renderer registry and IGraphicsRenderer::TransformWindowToLogical (inverse for Mouse::SetPosition); without a registration or with a false answer coordinates pass through unchanged.
concepts.note: The sibling input-model page carries the current per-family table; the older three-tier SDL-renderer/SDL-window ordering no longer exists.

concepts.text: Per-family input mapping: SDL_RENDERER delegates to SDL's logical presentation; EasyGL, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU and WebGPU map through the presented rectangle and return false in a bar; Vulkan answers true everywhere; DirectX 11/12 and FreeDirect implement the transform but never register; DirectX 9, Metal and the CPU renderers pass through.
concepts.note: The older matrix (EasyGL fixed-height only, Vulkan raw) is stale; the input-model page records the current reading.

concepts.text: An immediate Mouse::SetPosition then GetState round trip is a weak test because it can pass through the stored logical value even if the physical warp is wrong; stronger evidence injects physical motion into a scaled presentation.

The registry is one function-local static unordered_map<WindowId, IGraphicsRenderer*>: registration overwrites by key, unregistration erases by id without an ownership check, and there is no synchronisation.
concepts.note: Keyed by the platform WindowId, not a toolkit window pointer.

concepts.text: Registration must be the last constructor step because a throwing constructor never runs its destructor; EasyGL and OpenGL4 now register last, so the older dangling-entry risk from early EasyGL registration is gone.
tokens: Registration must be the last constructor step

concepts.text: Two devices attached to one borrowed window fight over the registry entry (the second overwrites, destroying the first removes the second's); no test covers constructor failure after registration, duplicate attachment or concurrent access, and CNA needs an ownership decision here.
tokens: Two devices attached to the same borrowed window

concepts.text: CnaPresentationMode has five values and defaults to Letterbox (the only XNA-faithful mode) both on the manager and in GraphicsRendererCreateArgs; descriptions giving fixed-height as the construction default are stale; the manager applies the mode before Reset.
tokens: Both the manager property and the renderer-create argument default to
concepts.note: Default corrected to Letterbox.

concepts.text: EasyGL and OpenGL4 implement all five modes through the shared GlPresentationSurfaceState transform, not only fixed-height width derivation.
Vulkan, WebGPU, SDL_GPU, DirectX 11, DirectX 12, Metal and FNA3D compute a presented rectangle per mode and override GetDefaultViewportRect; DirectX 9 only stores the value.
tokens: Stores the value; no presentation geometry override

concepts.text: SDL_RENDERER maps the five modes onto SDL logical presentation, computing the width itself for the fixed-height mode.
Canvas stores the mode and changes output width only for the fixed-height mode; FreeDirect stores the mode while the wrapped free-direct presenter hard-codes letterbox.
Software, Headless, PortableGL and Stub treat the mode as a no-op: there is no compositor for bar or crop semantics.

Portable code configures the manager before initialisation, uses NativeBackBuffer when physical readback coordinates matter, and treats an enum round trip as no evidence of letterbox, crop or stretch output.
tokens: An enum round trip through the property proves nothing about output

concepts.text: PresentInterval maps to 0/1/2 and every Reset forwards it through SetSwapInterval; the manager's Boolean reaches only 0 or 1, and 2 needs PreparingDeviceSettings; GetSwapIntervalEXT reports the last request on DirectX 11/12, EasyGL, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU and Vulkan.
EasyGL and OpenGL4 pass the exact integer to the platform GL context's swap-interval call at construction and reset.
Vulkan maps intervals to present modes with fallbacks and now rebuilds its swapchain when the interval changes at run time; interval 2 is not half-rate.
concepts.note: The runtime hook is no longer a no-op.

concepts.text: DirectX 11 and 12 pass the exact interval to DXGI Present, so 2 waits two vertical blanks; they do not collapse positive values to plain vsync. WebGPU, SDL_GPU and Metal do treat 2 as 1.
concepts.note: Older text grouped Direct3D 11/12 with the collapsing families.

concepts.text: DirectX 9 maps 0/1/2 to D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_IMMEDIATE/ONE/TWO and applies it through a device reset.
SDL_RENDERER collapses a positive interval to 1 at construction; at run time it passes the integer to SDL_SetRenderVSync and falls back to 1 if refused.
Canvas, FreeDirect, the DOM families, Software, Headless, PortableGL, Stub and GDI (empty override) have no display-interval implementation while the public property still changes.

Game constructs its first renderer before derived-game configuration, so a family consuming only the construction argument would keep the default; at 009d40f5 Reset forwards every part of the request through a hook.
tokens: before a derived game's constructor has run

concepts.text: No test times half-refresh presentation against ordinary vsync on any family; the registered interval tests check storage, forwarding and survival.
tokens: No test found times half-refresh presentation

concepts.section: Backbuffer format, depth format, and fullscreen
concepts.text: Reset normalises requested formats through the renderer, then applies window and virtual resolution inside a rollback block that restores presentation, adapter, touch dimensions and window before rethrowing; format update, MSAA and swap interval follow afterwards (in that order) and are not rolled back.
concepts.note: Order corrected: UpdatePresentationFormatEXT runs before ApplyMultiSampleCount and SetSwapInterval.

concepts.section: Backbuffer format, depth format, and fullscreen
concepts.text: Ten families override UpdatePresentationFormatEXT (not only DirectX 9), and fixed-format families override the applied-format queries so PresentationParameters reports Color and the real depth plane; families keeping the echo default can still report a format their 2D target lacks.
concepts.note: Older text: only D3D9 overrode the format-update hook.

concepts.section: Backbuffer format, depth format, and fullscreen
concepts.text: DirectX 9 maps requested colour and depth formats natively and applies them through a device reset; DirectX 11/12 use fixed colour, report Color, and never request DXGI exclusive full screen.
tokens: DirectX 9 honours real formats through a device reset

concepts.section: Backbuffer format, depth format, and fullscreen
concepts.text: Vulkan, WebGPU and SDL_GPU choose surface formats independently of the XNA enums; Vulkan reports Color and the depth it created, and its back buffer always owns depth.

concepts.section: Backbuffer format, depth format, and fullscreen
concepts.text: EasyGL's multisample back-buffer framebuffer now follows the selected DepthFormat (including stencil) rather than a fixed Depth24 without stencil; its colour stays RGBA8.
tokens: rebuilds its colour and depth(-stencil) renderbuffers

concepts.section: Backbuffer format, depth format, and fullscreen
concepts.text: The 2D families have no default depth or stencil attachment and Software keeps fixed CPU arrays; full screen for them is a window or browser concern.

concepts.text: A full-screen failure is not cleared and ignored at 009d40f5: on SDL3 a refused request throws PlatformException and Reset rolls back; IsFullScreen is still requested state rather than proof.
tokens: A full-screen request is not silently swallowed
concepts.note: Carried on the page as the corrected fact.

concepts.text: ReadBackbuffer promises tightly packed top-left RGBA8 and throws by default.
tokens: top-left origin and throws by default

concepts.text: GetBackBufferData throws under Reach, rejects a null destination, a negative startIndex, non-positive elementCount and overflow, refuses while any render target is bound, takes its region from PresentationParameters and requires elementCount to match the pixel count exactly.
tokens: while any render target is bound
concepts.note: Older text: no negative-start or overflow check and elementCount < width*height.

concepts.text: Physical back-buffer families: Vulkan, WebGPU, SDL_GPU, DirectX 9/11/12 and FNA3D read the swapchain or back-buffer resource; logical and physical sizes can diverge under scaling.
concepts.note: DirectX 12 and SDL_GPU no longer refuse.

concepts.text: EasyGL, OpenGL4, Software, GDI, PortableGL, SDL_RENDERER, Direct2D, FreeDirect and Canvas read their current drawing surface, but through the public API a bound target makes GetBackBufferData throw first.

Headless no longer fabricates a frame from the last clear colour: its ReadBackbuffer throws NotSupportedException after the public validation; Metal refuses readback and Stub inherits the throwing default.
concepts.note: The synthetic fill was removed (REMED-GFX-162).

concepts.text: There is no capability query for readback; a portable test names the family, source image, coordinate space and oracle.
tokens: There is no capability member for readback

concepts.text: Resource-side defaults (targets, effects, queries, buffers, textures) are where most reduced fallbacks and null results live.
IRenderTargetRenderer::GetMultiSampleCount defaults to 0 and HasRealDepthBuffer echoes the request; applied sample count and real attachment presence are stronger facts than constructor arguments.

IOcclusionQueryRenderer is fully pure virtual (plus PixelCountIsPreciseEXT) but its factory is optional; IEffectRenderer requires compile/bind/unbind/status while uniform and texture setters default to no-ops, so a valid program can drop parameters.
tokens: the effect uniform and texture setters

concepts.text: Dynamic buffers use the same renderer factory as static ones (CreateVertexBuffer has no dynamic parameter), so streaming intent reaches the renderer only through each upload's SetDataOptions.
SetDataWithOptions overrides at 009d40f5: DirectX 9/11/12, EasyGL, FNA3D, Headless, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU, Software and WebGPU; Vulkan inherits the default and WebGPU ignores the option.
The dynamic buffers' options-taking SetData wrappers now refresh the CPU shadow through the shared upload routine; the earlier stale-shadow defect is absent.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: VertexBuffer::UploadValidatedData writes cpuShadow_ before every renderer upload, options or not, and IndexBuffer does the same; the page states the current rule.

concepts.text: Every upload submits the whole logical buffer because the renderer contract has no destination offset; Discard zero-fills the shadow and never-written bytes read as zero.
tokens: Whole-buffer submission is a deliberate cost trade

concepts.text: SetVertexDeclaration is pure virtual and called before every upload with the complete declaration; a family translates it, stores it for draw-time validation or rejects it.
The effect-aware draw default discards GpuDrawParams and enters a coloured draw; stock-program families now refuse a declaration that cannot feed the selected program instead of drawing coloured.

Instancing has a throwing default; the shared code transports up to sixteen bindings by value with slot, buffer, declaration, stride, element offset and instance frequency, and deferred families must copy rather than re-read public bindings at replay.

More than one stream of the same input rate requires MultiStreamVertexInput, so the portable subset is one per-vertex plus one per-instance stream; ranges are validated only for streams the program reads.
tokens: one per-vertex plus one per-instance stream

concepts.text: Instancing implementers at 009d40f5: DirectX 9/11/12, EasyGL (not ES 2.0), FNA3D, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU, Software, Vulkan, WebGPU; SDL_GPU no longer inherits a throwing callback; Headless records without rasterising.

UpdatePixelsLevel defaults to a no-op but every family except Stub overrides it: SDL_RENDERER, Canvas and FreeDirect throw above level 0, Software stores declared levels, GPU families upload real mips; SDL_GPU no longer reaches the discarding default.
concepts.note: Older text: SDL GPU silently discarded higher levels and Software discarded them.

concepts.text: WebGPU regenerates mip chains where other families do not, which can overwrite authored upper levels; that divergence is documented on the WebGPU page.

Texture, cube and volume readback return true only for a complete region; the shared layer converts only on true and otherwise throws NotSupportedException without touching the destination, because a no-op default used to fabricate transparent black.
Per-family native volume/cube transfer routes differ; Headless refuses rather than manufacturing pixels, and shared fixtures distinguish slices, faces, sub-rectangles, mips and untouched sentinels.

target.evidence: modules/renderers/*/src (per-family cube/volume GetData not individually traced)

concepts.note: The page states the contract; the per-family route list was not re-traced.

concepts.text: RenderTargetCube inherits TextureCube uploads; acceptance is decided by the family through the completion contract, so an unsupported upload throws rather than being discarded.
Families with deferred work finalise the outgoing face or target before another becomes active; EasyGL now finalises the old face when switching faces of one cube.
concepts.note: Older text: same-cube face switches could skip finalisation.

concepts.text: Binding, clearing and viewport/scissor are shared device transactions followed by family-specific native operations.

All binding overloads normalise into RenderTargetBindingDescriptor entries; the first descriptor controls viewport, scissor and discard; the shared layer rejects null, disposed, foreign, sliced, mismatched and duplicate targets before the renderer call.
The duplicate check compares resources, so two faces of one cube in one set are refused; cube-in-MRT and Metal multi-target refusals happen in the families.
tokens: including two faces of one cube

concepts.text: CNA now returns immediately for an unchanged binding set (XNA semantics), so rebinding the same DiscardContents target no longer clears it again.
tokens: Rebinding the same set is a no-op
concepts.note: Older text said there was no redundant-binding early return; the page states the corrected fact.

concepts.text: PreserveContents and PlatformContents both map to preserve; exact DiscardContents triggers the shared black clear of colour plus each depth/stencil plane the first descriptor really has; back-buffer usage is outside this policy.

WebGPU and Software no longer reject multi-target sets (two to four and up to four); stock effects write attachment 0 only, so a true MRT answer needs a multi-target bind and an oracle for every output.
tokens: The stock effects write attachment 0 only

concepts.text: GraphicsDevice converts the colour once and dispatches one of seven pure-virtual clear entry points; a request for a depth or stencil plane that does not exist throws InvalidOperationException instead of being masked, while Clear(Color) uses the available aspects.
concepts.note: Older text said unavailable aspects are masked.

concepts.text: Vulkan, WebGPU and SDL_GPU preserve clear ordering across deferred pass segments.
tokens: Recorded and replayed in submission order

concepts.text: DirectX 11/12 issue immediate native clears; DirectX 9 now gates depth/stencil clear flags by the active target's depth format, not the back-buffer format.
EasyGL's colour-only clear formerly added the GL depth bit without forcing depth writes, so a target-only clear could clear or keep depth depending on earlier state.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: EasyGLRenderer::Clear is colour only at 009d40f5 (REMED-GFX-142 comment) and also neutralises scissor and colour masks; EasyGL_ClearOverloads exercises the overloads. Taught as a historical case on the EasyGL page.

concepts.text: SDL_RENDERER, Canvas and FreeDirect have no depth/stencil plane, so Clear(Color) sends colour only and an explicit depth/stencil request throws in the device before any 2D hook.
tokens: throws in the device before any 2D hook is reached

concepts.text: Software clears colour, depth and stencil in CPU arrays; Headless records without attachment semantics.
There is no capability for clear aspect selectivity or ordering; a test must prime and observe each aspect after intervening work.
tokens: No capability member reports whether a clear is aspect-selective

concepts.text: The device validates, maps logical to presentation coordinates, calls the renderer hook and only then commits the public viewport or scissor; scissor enable arrives separately in ApplyRasterizerState, so a getter round trip proves bookkeeping only.
tokens: Scissor enable never travels with the rectangle
concepts.note: Added validation and logical-to-presentation mapping present at 009d40f5.

concepts.text: Vulkan, WebGPU and SDL_GPU capture viewport and scissor per deferred command; EasyGL and OpenGL4 apply them immediately with Y-flips against the active target height.
EasyGL's SpriteBatch now keeps a custom sub-viewport and projects from its logical size; the older claim that it resets to the full target and never restores is stale.
DirectX 12 now applies the effective viewport and scissor on every draw, including sprite batches; the full-target scissor defect is fixed.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: every DirectX 12 draw route sets GetEffectiveViewportEXT and GetEffectiveScissorEXT (DX-201, REMED-GFX-064); the page states the current behaviour.

concepts.text: SDL_RENDERER has no viewport hook and applies any non-empty scissor rectangle as its clip rectangle regardless of ScissorTestEnable.
Software now snapshots the viewport transform and a framebuffer-viewport-scissor clip per draw for 2D and 3D; the claim that its 3D NDC mapping spans the full framebuffer is stale.
Canvas and FreeDirect implement neither viewport nor scissor; Headless validates and traces without rasterising.

Target switches reset viewport and scissor to the destination; construction sets full rectangles; Present and a size-preserving reset keep custom values because UpdateViewportFromWindow resets only on a change; no capability reports either feature.

GraphicsCapability has 19 members; the shared default answers true except multi-stream input, compiled effects and the two float render-target members, with stencil delegated; that optimistic polarity makes a true answer meaningful only where the family audited the operation.
concepts.note: Older text listed 13 members with only multi-stream false.

concepts.text: Recorded MRT contradiction (Headless, Software, WebGPU): Software and WebGPU now bind real multi-target sets and Headless traces; the device answers false under Reach everywhere.
Recorded occlusion-query contradiction: WebGPU and Software now return real counts, SDL_GPU answers false and refuses creation, Headless is synthetic (always one visible sample).
Recorded custom-effects contradiction on WebGPU is closed: WebGPU compiles WGSL ShaderEffect source.
Recorded instancing contradiction: SDL_GPU overrides the instanced route; Headless still records only.
Recorded MSAA contradiction: Software now applies a back-buffer sample count; several families negotiate requests down, so the applied MultiSampleCount is the stronger fact.
Recorded anisotropy contradiction: SDL_GPU clamps and applies it, Software honours it against a device cap; DirectX 9 still inherits the default answer and forwards the value unclamped.
The defensible sequence for any capability is query, factory, operation, engagement, then a discriminating behavioural or pixel oracle.

SetContextRecoveryEnabled changes shared texture-shadow policy before calling the renderer hook; disabling it lets a full upload drop CPU pixels so later partial updates or readback can fail, re-enabling reconstructs nothing, and the header's 'before device initialization' cannot be literal.
Seven families override the recovery hook (DirectX 9/11/12, Direct2D, EasyGL, GDI, WebGPU), not only EasyGL.

F9 and F10 key-down events pass through input first and then call DebugSimulateContextLoss/DebugRestoreContext; EasyGL, DirectX 9/11/12, Direct2D and WebGPU have non-empty overrides; others are no-ops.
concepts.note: Current family list recorded on the sibling page.

concepts.text: SetStringMarkerEXT is a no-op by default; DirectX 9, FNA3D, GDI, Metal, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU, Vulkan and WebGPU override it, and a successful call does not prove a native marker was emitted.
tokens: SetStringMarkerEXT is a no-op by default

concepts.text: A configure-time identity maps to one of 21 families, five EasyGL identities share one family, and platform and dependency gates run before the registry is generated.

There is no single global CreateGraphicsRenderer any more: each family declares its factory in its own namespace and the registry reaches it through GraphicsRendererDescriptor::create; the old shared declaration was removed because it allowed colliding global definitions.
concepts.note: Older text: the selected module provides exactly one global CreateGraphicsRenderer.

concepts.text: GraphicsRendererCreateArgs carries the surface snapshot, the requested platform service, virtual size, presentation mode, recovery policy, MSAA count, swap interval, back-buffer and depth formats, full-screen flag, profile and a device-event callback; field presence is not a promise that a family consumes it.
tokens: Field presence is not a promise

concepts.text: Historical audit narration of task numbers and repaired defaults explains three live hazards: permissive defaults allowed plausible reduced draws, CPU-shadow round trips masked missing GPU uploads, and direct helper tests bypassed the public coordinate route.
concepts.note: Campaign narrative; the three hazards it names are each represented by current concepts (reduced fallbacks, CPU-shadow evidence caveat, input-mapping test caveat).

concepts.text: Application guidance: choose a renderer by operations and evidence, treat capability answers as preflight hints, keep resources device-scoped, separate logical from physical coordinates, and expect custom effects, MRT, queries, instancing and readback to need family-specific qualification.
tokens: treat capability answers as preflight hints

concepts.text: A complete renderer claim for one operation needs a reachable factory, shared public routing, applied state, correct target and lifetime behaviour, engagement evidence and a discriminating oracle.
tokens: overriding a virtual is only the start

issues.text: GameWindow keeps the borrowed IPlatformWindow* it received in the Game constructor after the game explicitly disposes the GraphicsDevice (which destroys that window); nothing rebinds or clears it, so later GameWindow property calls can reach a destroyed platform window.

ShaderEffect::SetTexture(int, TextureCube&) and SetTexture(int, Texture3D&) pass texture.GetRenderer(), which dereferences a null renderer handle when the renderer's cube or volume factory returned null.

SDL_RENDERER applies any non-empty ScissorRectangle as its SDL clip rectangle regardless of RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable (it has no ApplyRasterizerState override), so a game that sets a scissor rectangle with the test disabled is still clipped.

The WindowId-to-renderer registry has no ownership check or synchronisation: two devices attached to one borrowed window overwrite each other's entry and destroying one removes the other's; no test covers duplicate attachment, constructor failure after registration or concurrent lookup.
TextInputEXT and Mouse window slots are process-wide with last-writer semantics, so two live GraphicsDevices replace each other's input target; the multi-device lifecycle is untested.
No test on any family times PresentInterval::Two (half-refresh) against ordinary vsync; the registered interval tests check storage, forwarding and survival only.

FREEDIRECT stores the presentation mode but the wrapped free-direct presenter hard-codes letterbox; Stretch, Overscan and NativeBackBuffer cannot reach physical output. CANVAS changes output only for FixedHeightDynamicWidth and DIRECTX9 has no presentation-geometry override.
CANVAS and FREEDIRECT override neither SetViewport nor SetScissorRect, so GraphicsDevice.Viewport and ScissorRectangle have no effect on those 2D renderers.

DIRECTX9 inherits the default true AnisotropicFiltering answer and forwards the requested MaxAnisotropy to D3DSAMP_MAXANISOTROPY without clamping to the device's MaxAnisotropy cap in ApplySamplerState (the compiled-effect path does consult caps).
METAL refuses back-buffer readback outright (disabled after a historical macOS run returned clear-colour-only data); GetBackBufferData throws NotSupportedException there.

CNA's docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md says destructor cleanup suppresses ResourceDestroyed, but GraphicsResource::Dispose(false) raises it whenever the device lifetime token is alive (documentation staleness inside CNA).

Stale source comments: GraphicsRendererCreateArgs::deviceEventCallback says nine of ten renderers never call it (six families do); GraphicsDevice::SetContextRecoveryEnabled says it must be called before the device is initialised (impossible for a member); GetDefaultViewportRect names a retired renderer's override as the reference implementation.
Former defect: options-taking DynamicVertexBuffer/DynamicIndexBuffer SetData did not refresh the CPU shadow; at 009d40f5 every upload goes through UploadValidatedData, which writes the shadow first.
Former defect: HEADLESS ReadBackbuffer filled the destination with the last clear colour; at 009d40f5 it throws NotSupportedException (REMED-GFX-162) and DirectX 12 and SDL_GPU implement readback.
Former defect: DIRECTX12 installed a full-target scissor on every draw, making scissored sprite drawing a no-op; at 009d40f5 every draw route uses GetEffectiveScissorEXT (DX-201).

Former defect: DIRECTX9 gated depth/stencil clear flags by the back-buffer format even with a differently formatted target bound; at 009d40f5 activeDepthStencilFormatOrdinal_ follows every target bind.
